Project: Kubernetes. Upgrade being assessed: 1.23 -> 1.29.
This change was introduced in release 1.27. Source: Kubernetes v1.27.0 CHANGELOG (official_changelog). Section: v1.27.0 / Changes by Kind / Deprecation.
Version facts from package metadata for this release (authoritative for version numbers): none

ITEM:
<<<
Support for the alpha seccomp annotations seccomp.security.alpha.kubernetes.io/pod and container.seccomp.security.alpha.kubernetes.io were deprecated since v1.19, now have been completely removed. The seccomp fields are no longer auto-populated when pods with seccomp annotations are created. Pods should use the corresponding pod or container securityContext.seccompProfile field instead.
>>>

PARENT CONTEXT (same section, for disambiguation only):
<<<
v1.27.0 / Changes by Kind / Deprecation: Added a warning response when handling requests that set the deprecated spec.externalID field for a Node. Added warnings to the Services API. Kubernetes now warns for Services in the case of: - IPv4 addresses with leading zeros - IPv6 address in non-canonical format (RFC 5952) Support for the alpha seccomp annotations seccomp.security.alpha.kubernetes.io/pod and container.seccomp.security.alpha.kubernetes.io were deprecated since v1.19, now have been completely removed. The seccomp fields are no longer auto-populated when pods with seccomp annotations are created. Pods should use the corresponding pod or container securityContext.seccompProfile field instead. The SecurityContextDeny admission plugin is going deprecated and will be removed in future versions.
>>>

Decide the disposition:
- "risk": the item describes something that can break an app/deployment, require migration work, or create operational risk.
- "context": it is accurate but needs no action at 1.29 (no user action required, deprecated-but-working, additive feature). Give the reason.

For "risk", produce one or more risk paths. Use separate paths for separate symbols/APIs when they can be checked independently. Hard rules:
1. Every condition has at least one quote copied EXACTLY, character for character, from ITEM or PARENT CONTEXT (contiguous span, 3-40 words, no ellipses, no added words). Do not fix typos or formatting.
2. Each path has exactly one condition with category "version" stating that the upgrade crosses release 1.27 (quote the text that ties the change to this release, or the change statement itself), and at least one application/deployment condition (category api_usage, configuration, dependency, runtime, deployment, database, behavior or test_coverage) describing what the app or deployment must use/have for the risk to apply.
3. If the text does not state something you need, do not assert it: use role "uncertain" and explain in ambiguities. derived_by: "extraction" when the text states the fact; for an application/deployment condition ("the application uses X"), use "extraction" when the text names X as the thing affected by the change. Use "inference" only when you infer an affected symbol, scope or impact that the text does not name. Only add ambiguities for real gaps or conflicts in the text, not for the general fact that a specific application has not been inspected.
4. role: "required" (must hold), "alternative" (any one of the alternatives suffices), "optional" (raises impact), "disqualifying" (if it holds, the risk does NOT apply, e.g. not using the new opt-in API), "uncertain".
5. operator/expected_value must be checkable: e.g. operator "present" with expected_value the literal symbol; "less_than" with a version; "equals" with a setting value. expected_value is a string.
6. If a replacement API/setting/version is named, put the migration step in suggested_actions and add a condition for any behavior that differs in the replacement when the text states one.
7. search_queries: for app-side conditions with a literal symbol, give ripgrep regexes (tool "ripgrep"), kubectl commands (tool "kubectl") or SQL (tool "sql") that would find usage. Empty list if no literal symbol.
8. primary_symbol: the most specific identifier of the change (full apiVersion string like "policy/v1beta1", setting name, function, flag, or runtime name like "Python"/"Node.js"). symbols: all identifiers involved.
9. risk_level rubric: critical = upgrade fails or data is at risk for most users meeting the conditions (e.g. unsupported runtime/database version, removed API version that stops serving); high = code or config meeting the conditions breaks at upgrade; medium = behavior change or migration with a clear workaround; low = edge case, cosmetic, or warning-only.
10. fires_at: "upgrade" (at upgrade time), "first_use" (when a feature is first exercised), "rotation" (on credential/password rotation), "rollout" (on deployment rollout), "future_removal" (deprecated now, removed later).
11. applies_to: fill upgrade_method (e.g. "pg_upgrade", "dump/restore"), cluster_type, or from_versions (a version specifier like "<3.1") ONLY if the text restricts applicability; otherwise null.
Do not output confidence.

paths.description: The alpha seccomp annotations seccomp.security.alpha.kubernetes.io/pod and container.seccomp.security.alpha.kubernetes.io have been completely removed. Seccomp fields are no longer auto-populated from these annotations when pods are created, so pods that depend on them need migration to the securityContext.seccompProfile field.

conditions.statement: The upgrade from 1.23 to 1.29 crosses release 1.27, in which the alpha seccomp annotations were removed.
conditions.relevance: Ties the removal to release 1.27, which the upgrade from 1.23 to 1.29 crosses.

conditions.statement: Application pods use the alpha seccomp annotation seccomp.security.alpha.kubernetes.io/pod or container.seccomp.security.alpha.kubernetes.io.
conditions.relevance: The risk applies only to pods that set the removed alpha seccomp annotations.

search_queries.query: kubectl get pods --all-namespaces -o yaml | grep seccomp.security.alpha.kubernetes.io

conditions.statement: Pods with seccomp annotations no longer get their seccomp fields auto-populated when created.
quotes: The seccomp fields are no longer auto-populated when pods with seccomp annotations are created.
conditions.relevance: Pods that rely on the auto-populated seccomp fields will no longer receive them after the upgrade.
ambiguities: The text does not state what runtime behavior results for pods whose seccomp fields are no longer populated.

conditions.statement: Pods already set the securityContext.seccompProfile field instead of the removed annotations.
quotes: Pods should use the corresponding pod or container securityContext.seccompProfile field instead.
conditions.relevance: If pods already use the securityContext.seccompProfile field, the removal of the annotations does not affect them.

suggested_actions: Find pods and pod templates that set seccomp.security.alpha.kubernetes.io/pod or container.seccomp.security.alpha.kubernetes.io annotations.
Replace these annotations with the pod or container securityContext.seccompProfile field before upgrading.
